title: SRE standards: SLOs, error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, and runbooks
author: Ari Chen
content:
Summary
This document defines Redwood Inference SRE standards for Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, capacity planning guidance, reliability initiatives, incident review expectations, operational tooling requirements, and canonical runbooks. The goal is to provide a consistent, production-grade approach for teams that operate services on the Redwood platform.

Scope
Applies to all customer-facing inference services (hosted API surface), control plane services (routing, metering), and core internal systems that impact customer SLOs (inference-gateway, model-router, kv-cache-service, allocator, telemetry-pipeline). Not intended for ephemeral developer tooling.

1) Principles and definitions
- SLI (Service Level Indicator): a measured signal (success rate, latency percentile, queue depth) used to evaluate SLO compliance.
- SLO (Service Level Objective): target level for an SLI over a rolling measurement window (usually 30d).
- Error budget: 1 - SLO; how much unreliability is allowed over the measurement window. Error budget consumption drives risk-based decisions (deployments, config changes).
- Blameless postmortem: culture expectation after incidents; root cause and corrective actions focused on systemic improvement.

2) SLO catalog and required defaults
- Every production service MUST publish an SLO and owner in the internal SLO registry. Minimum required SLOs (defaults for commonly used services):

| SLO ID | Service | SLI | SLO (30d window) | Measurement | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| SLO-100 | inference-gateway | successful requests (2xx) | 99.95% | rolling 30d | inference-sre@redwood.com |
| SLO-200 | model-router | successful routing | 99.9% | rolling 30d | runtime-team@redwood.com |
| SLO-300 | kv-cache-service | P95 read latency | < 25ms | rolling 30d | cache-team@redwood.com |
| SLO-400 | telemetry-pipeline | event processing success | 99.5% | rolling 30d | telemetry@redwood.com |

Notes:
- Latency SLOs should use P95 for user-facing interactive paths and P99 for high-criticality flows.
- Availability SLOs should exclude planned maintenance if customers were given prior notice and appropriate mitigation.

3) Error budget policy and operational playbook
- Error budget calculation: error_budget_remaining = 1 - (observed_error_rate over window).
- Tiers and automated responses:
  - Green (>= 75% error budget remaining): Normal ops. Deployments permitted. No additional approvals required.
  - Yellow (25% - 75% remaining): Teams must schedule reduced-risk releases (e.g., smaller canaries). Notify product/security if changes touch sensitive flows.
  - Red (< 25% remaining): Freeze risky changes. All production deployments require explicit approval from SRE lead. Prepare mitigation runbooks and raise a cross-functional review.
  - Critical burn (> 5% remaining and burn rate projected to exhaust budget within 24h): Immediate incident triage and possible rollback of recent rollouts. Page on-call and assign responder.

- Deployment gating: CI deploy job must query the SLO registry and abort automated deploys if service is in Red. Example (bash):
  - curl -s https://internal-api.redwood/slo-registry/service/inference-gateway | jq .error_budget_remaining
  - if value < 0.25 then exit 1

4) Capacity planning guidance
- Goal: maintain >= 4x headroom for typical growth and 15% buffer for diurnal peaks while meeting SLOs.
- Inputs: historical QPS, 95th percentile request size, model token generation distribution, per-token cost and latency curves, tail-latency profile by seq-length.
- Capacity runbook steps (quarterly):
  1. Export last 90 days of traffic (qps by minute) and 95/99 latency percentiles by model and route.
  2. Model growth scenarios (conservative +25% / aggressive +50% over next quarter).
  3. Simulate scheduling using the runtime cost model (batching efficiency curves at different concurrency).
  4. Produce capacity plan: target GPU counts per region, pre-provision windows, and autoscaling thresholds.
  5. Publish plan to infra channel and schedule procurement for Dedicated clusters if expected headroom dips below 2x.

- Autoscaling policy template (recommended):
  - scale-out: trigger when 1-minute moving average CPU/GPU util > 70% OR queue length > 5x baseline for more than 120s.
  - scale-in: cool down min 10 minutes after scale-out, only if util < 40% and queue length <= baseline.

5) Reliability initiatives and backlog prioritization
- Every SRE team must maintain a reliability backlog with items classified as: Technical debt, Instrumentation, Resiliency features, Capacity investments.
- Quarterly reliability themes (example roadmap entry):
  - Q1: KV-cache region failover and cold-warm cache priming (reduce 99th latency).
  - Q2: Continuous chaos testing for router/allocator and automated recovery playbooks.

KPIs to track for initiatives: error budget burn rate, reduction in incident MTTR, percentage of incidents with action items closed within 30 days.

6) Incident review standards and postmortems
- All incidents that cross a Severity 2 threshold or consume > 10% of a service’s weekly error budget require a postmortem within 72 hours.
- Minimum postmortem template (must be included in the postmortem doc):
  1. Summary (1-2 sentences)
  2. Timeline (UTC timestamps)
  3. Impact (customers affected, SLO impact, cost)
  4. Root cause analysis (code, config, capacity, change)
  5. Action items (owner, due date, verification steps)
  6. Lessons learned and follow-ups
- Postmortem review: schedule a 30–60 minute blameless review with stakeholders within 7 days. Ensure action items are added to the reliability backlog.

7) Operational tooling standards
- Alerting:
  - Alerts must be actionable and tied to runbooks. Each alert must include: runbook link, on-call rotation, required severity, and ticket template.
  - Avoid high-cardinality metric alerts (use aggregation or dimensions).
- Dashboards:
  - Standard dashboards per service: Overview (traffic, success rate, latency p50/p95/p99, error budget remaining), Capacity (utilization, queue depth, pod/gpu counts), Recent deploys and trace sampling.
- Tracing and structured logs:
  - All requests must carry a trace-id header (x-trace-id) from edge to backend and be sampled at least 0.5% by default; 100% sampling for error responses. Logs must be structured JSON with fields: timestamp, trace_id, request_id, service, route, latency_ms, status_code, user_id (when present).
- Automation and SLO-driven CI gates:
  - CI should call SLO API and block or flag deploys based on error budget state (see error budget policy).

8) Canonical runbooks (examples)
- Runbook: inference-gateway high 5xx rate
  1. Pager: on-call for inference-gateway.
  2. Quick triage: check Service Overview dashboard -> error rate timeline, recent deploys, and alert context.
  3. Rollback path: if incident started within 30 minutes of a deploy, consider immediate rollback via deploy pipeline (ci-deploy rollback --service inference-gateway --to last-stable).
  4. Traffic mitigation: enable model-router fallback rule to route 20% traffic to secondary cluster: 
     - curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"route":"inference-gateway","policy":"split","split":{"primary":80,"secondary":20}}' https://internal-api.redwood/router/config
  5. Cache priming: warm kv-cache keys for top 50 models using cache-prime tool: cache-prime --service kv-cache-service --models top50 --parallel 8
  6. Post-incident: run postmortem per template and run through action item verification.

- Runbook: allocation saturation / GPU queueing
  1. Pager: allocator on-call.
  2. Triage: check allocator dashboard -> pending jobs, avg wait time, GPU util by node.
  3. Short-term mitigation: increase burst capacity (if policy allows) via infra console or toggle autoscaling cap: infra-cli set-burst-cap --cluster <cluster> --percent 20
  4. If burst not available, place low-priority batch workloads into delayed queue to free capacity: infra-cli reclassify-workloads --priority batch --delay 60m
  5. Post-incident: update capacity plan and schedule scale-up with cloud procurement if headroom < 2x.

9) Metrics, alerts and example alert rules
- Example Prometheus alert (P95 latency breach):
  - ALERT InferenceGatewayP95LatencyHigh
    IF histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service=~"inference-gateway"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.150
    FOR 5m
    LABELS { severity="page" }
    ANNOTATIONS { summary="inference-gateway P95 > 150ms", runbook="/confluence/eng-sre/inference-gateway-runbook" }

- Example error budget burn alert:
  - ALERT ErrorBudgetBurnHigh
    IF slo_error_budget_burn_rate{service="inference-gateway"} > 1.2
    FOR 10m
    LABELS { severity="page" }
    ANNOTATIONS { summary="Error budget burn > 120% (projected exhaustion)", runbook="/confluence/eng-sre/sre-slos-capacity-error-budgets-and-runbooks" }

10) Ownership and escalation
- SLO owner: engineering team responsible for the service (published in SLO registry).
- On-call rotations: each service must list primary and secondary on-call in the runbook header. Escalation policy: page primary -> after 10m escalate to secondary -> after 20m escalate to SRE lead.

Appendix A — SLO registry fields (minimum)
- service_name (string)
- slo_id (string)
- sli_definition (string)
- slo_target (string)
- measurement_window (string)
- owner_email (string)
- runbook_link (string)

Appendix B — Example postmortem checklist
- Confirm timeline completeness
- Validate instrumentation and metrics used for RCA
- Identify reproducible steps for mitigation
- Ensure at least one corrective action that prevents recurrence
- Assign owners and due dates
